_README: OWNER: Engineer B. Shown only when /api/jobs finds no local match — the no-dead-ends path.
STATUS: real data. The placeholder TODO trends were replaced on 2026-08-08.
Every figure below comes from one primary source, retrieved directly:
Clackamas, Multnomah, and Washington Counties', published December 18, 2025. Spreadsheet:
GEOGRAPHY NOTE: this is OED's Portland tri-county area (Clackamas, Multnomah, Washington) — the
geography QualityInfo publishes as 'Portland Metro'. It is not the 7-county Portland-Vancouver-
Hillsboro MSA (no Clark, Columbia, Yamhill or Skamania counties). Say 'Portland metro' in the demo.
Regionwide baseline from the same table: 1,065,200 jobs in 2024 to 1,142,600 in 2034, +77,400 (+7%).
HONESTY CONTEXT for anyone demoing this: these are 10-year projections, not current conditions.
Portland metro nonfarm employment is currently FALLING — 1,235,200 in March 2025 to 1,202,900 in
March 2026 (about -32,000), per BLS Current Employment Statistics retrieved via FRED series
trend string below is worded as 'projected' with the 2024-2034 window attached.
No number here was estimated or rounded up beyond whole percentages taken from the source table.
The `resource` URL returned HTTP 200 on 2026-08-08 and its description matches what the page states.

sectors.name: Health Care & Social Assistance
sectors.trend: Projected to add about 18,700 jobs in the Portland metro between 2024 and 2034, a 14% increase — roughly double the region's projected 7% growth overall.
sectors.source: Oregon Employment Department, QualityInfo.org — Portland Tri-County Industry Employment Projections 2024-2034 (published Dec. 18, 2025)

sectors.name: Professional & Business Services
sectors.trend: Projected to add about 17,300 jobs in the Portland metro between 2024 and 2034 (11%), with professional and technical services accounting for 11,100 of that gain.
sectors.source: Oregon Employment Department, QualityInfo.org — Portland Tri-County Industry Employment Projections 2024-2034 (published Dec. 18, 2025)

sectors.name: Leisure & Hospitality
sectors.trend: Projected to add about 9,500 jobs in the Portland metro between 2024 and 2034, a 10% increase, most of it in food services and accommodation.
sectors.source: Oregon Employment Department, QualityInfo.org — Portland Tri-County Industry Employment Projections 2024-2034 (published Dec. 18, 2025)

sectors.name: Construction
sectors.trend: Projected to grow 11% in the Portland metro between 2024 and 2034, adding about 6,300 jobs, of which 4,100 are with specialty trade contractors.
sectors.source: Oregon Employment Department, QualityInfo.org — Portland Tri-County Industry Employment Projections 2024-2034 (published Dec. 18, 2025)

sectors.name: Transportation, Warehousing & Utilities
sectors.trend: Projected to add about 4,200 jobs in the Portland metro between 2024 and 2034 (9%), including 1,300 more courier and messenger jobs and 1,100 more in warehousing and storage.
sectors.source: Oregon Employment Department, QualityInfo.org — Portland Tri-County Industry Employment Projections 2024-2034 (published Dec. 18, 2025)

sectors.name: Information
sectors.trend: Projected to grow 9% in the Portland metro between 2024 and 2034, adding about 1,900 jobs, with software publishers alone accounting for 1,200 of them.
sectors.source: Oregon Employment Department, QualityInfo.org — Portland Tri-County Industry Employment Projections 2024-2034 (published Dec. 18, 2025)

sectors.name: Architectural & Engineering Services
sectors.trend: Projected to grow 23% in the Portland metro between 2024 and 2034, adding about 3,000 jobs — the fastest projected growth rate of any industry line in the region's projections table (it is counted within professional and business services above).
sectors.source: Oregon Employment Department, QualityInfo.org — Portland Tri-County Industry Employment Projections 2024-2034 (published Dec. 18, 2025)
